content: It outlines the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic interactions, potential additive effects, and clinical considerations for co-administration. 1. Methscopolamine may interact with glucagon, leading to increased toxicity due to additive effects on gastrointestinal motility inhibition. Co-administration with anticholinergic drugs and glucagon increases the risk of gastrointestinal adverse reactions. Avoid or consider alternative drugs. 2. Glycopyrronium tosylate (topical) and methscopolamine may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially causing additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 3. Pramlintide and methscopolamine may synergistically inhibit gastrointestinal motility, making their combination contraindicated. 4. Revecenacin and methscopolamine both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially leading to additive anticholinergic effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Methscopolamine reduces the effects of secretin by pharmacodynamic antagonism, which may cause a hyporesponse during stimulation testing. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 6. Sofpironium topical and methscopolamine may cause additive anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Methscopolamine and umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol (inhaled) may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Methscopolamine may potentiate the effects of abobotulinumtoxinA, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Methscopolamine and aclidinium both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Aluminum hydroxide decreases methscopolamine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Methscopolamine and amantadine may increase anticholinergic adverse effects due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Methscopolamine and amitriptyline both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Aripiprazole may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Methscopolamine and atropine both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Methscopolamine and belladonna alkaloids both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of clozapine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Clozapine may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Methscopolamine and dicyclomine both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Methscopolamine and donepezil may have opposing effects on cholinergic transmission, with donepezil increasing and methscopolamine decreasing cholinergic activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of haloperidol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Haloperidol may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Methscopolamine and ipratropium both reduce cholinergic transmission, but due to poor systemic absorption of ipratropium, interaction is unlikely at recommended dosages. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Methscopolamine and oxybutynin both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of risperidone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Risperidone may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Methscopolamine and tiotropium both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of ziprasidone by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Ziprasidone may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Methscopolamine and botulinum toxins (e.g., onabotulinumtoxinA, incobotulinumtoxinA) may have additive effects, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Methscopolamine and other anticholinergic agents (e.g., solifenacin, tolterodine) may cause additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Methscopolamine decreases the levels of thioridazine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption and through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Thioridazine may increase the effects of methscopolamine via pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Methscopolamine and tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., imipramine, nortriptyline) both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Methscopolamine and neuromuscular blocking agents (e.g., pancuronium, vecuronium) both reduce cholinergic transmission, potentially causing additive effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Methscopolamine and levodopa may interact, with anticholinergic agents potentially enhancing levodopa's therapeutic effects but exacerbating tardive dyskinesia. High doses of anticholinergics may reduce levodopa's effects by delaying gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor closely. This summary provides a professional interpretation of the drug interactions involving methscopolamine, emphasizing the need for caution, monitoring, and potential avoidance of certain combinations.
